slot.brief: A chain of connected blocks on rough surfaces or a massive rope pulled over a pulley; write free-body equations for each and solve for tension at a point or acceleration (symbolic multi-equation).

stem: A uniform rope of mass $M$ and length $L$ connects blocks $m_1$ and $m_2$ over an ideal pulley, with $m_2>m_1$. At a point a distance $x$ from $m_1$ along its vertical side, what is the rope tension?

verdicts.working: The system acceleration is \(a=\frac{(m_2-m_1)g}{m_1+m_2+M}\). For the block \(m_1\) and rope segment of mass \(Mx/L\), \(T=(m_1+Mx/L)(g+a)\), giving option B.

working:
$a=\dfrac{(m_2-m_1)g}{m_1+m_2+M}$. The block and rope segment up to the point have mass $m_1+Mx/L$ and accelerate upward. $T-(m_1+Mx/L)g=(m_1+Mx/L)a$. Hence $T=\dfrac{g\left(m_1+\dfrac{Mx}{L}\right)(2m_2+M)}{m_1+m_2+M}$.

Independent check: The system acceleration is \(a=\frac{(m_2-m_1)g}{m_1+m_2+M}\). For the block \(m_1\) and rope segment of mass \(Mx/L\), \(T=(m_1+Mx/L)(g+a)\), giving option B.
solution: The system acceleration is $$a=\frac{(m_2-m_1)g}{m_1+m_2+M}.$$ The block and rope segment up to the point, of mass $m_1+\frac{Mx}{L}$, accelerate upward, so $T=(m_1+\frac{Mx}{L})(g+a)=\dfrac{g\left(m_1+\dfrac{Mx}{L}\right)(2m_2+M)}{m_1+m_2+M}$.
